name: Chaport
tagline: A simple, affordable live chat widget with a scripted, rule-based chatbot builder — not a genuine AI agent, despite the category it gets compared in.
tldr: Chaport is a live chat widget for small businesses with a visual flow-builder chatbot — but the chatbot is rule-based (decision-tree and keyword-triggered), not an LLM-powered AI agent that generates novel responses from a knowledge base.

Pricing is genuinely affordable: Free (2 operators), Pro at $29/mo (4 operators, billed annually — $39 month-to-month), Unlimited at $99/mo (unlimited operators, billed annually — $129 month-to-month), with a 25% annual discount and a 14-day free Unlimited trial.

Company history is unusually unclear: some sources place founding in 2014 in Alhambra, California; more recent and numerous sources describe a 2016 founding by Dmitry Birukov and Pavel Potapov, now headquartered in Yoshkar-Ola, Russia. Neither account is a primary company filing, so treat both as unreconciled.

The chatbot builder is a genuine, functional visual tool — conversation flows, triggers, and branching reply options — but it requires manually building every conversation path rather than training automatically on your content the way a modern AI agent does.

Independent reviews are strongly positive for what the product actually is: a simple, affordable, easy-to-set-up live chat widget, with reviewers specifically praising value against pricier competitors like Intercom — but the review base is small (21 on G2) and several reviews are several years old, a sign of a product that hasn't seen the same recent attention as AI-native competitors.

Best for small businesses and solo operators that want a straightforward, cheap live chat widget with a scripted FAQ bot — not for any team specifically shopping for genuine AI-driven customer support automation.
keyFeatures: A visual chatbot builder for designing rule-based conversation flows with triggers and branching reply options — not a generative AI agent
Saved replies (Pro tier) and shared team saved replies (Unlimited tier) for consistent, fast agent responses
A multilingual widget that automatically detects a visitor's language and switches the interface to match, without a paid add-on
Auto-invitations, pre-chat forms, and an autoresponder for proactive and after-hours engagement
A basic knowledge base with an FAQ bot on the Unlimited tier, built on the same rule-based logic as the chatbot rather than an LLM
Teams, assignment rules, and custom fields for basic internal routing and organization on the Unlimited tier
REST and JavaScript APIs (Pro tier and above) plus a Zapier integration (Unlimited tier only) for external connectivity
Native desktop, web, and mobile apps for agents, alongside a dedicated WordPress plugin for website installation

faq.question: Is Chaport's chatbot powered by AI?
faq.answer: Not in the modern, generative sense. Chaport's chatbot is built with a visual flow builder using conversation triggers and branching reply options — a rule-based, decision-tree or keyword-recognition system, not a large-language-model agent that generates novel answers from your content. If you're specifically shopping for AI-driven, self-learning customer support automation, this isn't that; it's a scripted bot you build by hand, similar in spirit to older-generation chatbot tools from before the LLM era.

faq.question: How does Chaport's pricing compare to competitors?
faq.answer: It's genuinely affordable for what it does: Free for 2 operators, Pro at $29/month (annual) for 4 operators with saved replies and basic reporting, and Unlimited at $99/month (annual) for unlimited operators, chatbots, and a knowledge base. That undercuts most AI-native competitors substantially, but it's also not solving the same problem — you're paying less because you're getting a simpler, scripted product rather than a generative AI agent.

faq.question: Does Chaport support multiple languages?
faq.answer: Yes, and this is a genuine strength — the widget automatically detects a visitor's language and switches the interface to match, without requiring a separate paid translation add-on. This is more capable, natively, than several AI-focused competitors that rely on third-party translation integrations.

faq.question: Why is Chaport's company history unclear?
faq.answer: Sources conflict meaningfully: some describe a 2014 founding based in Alhambra, California, while more numerous and recent sources describe a 2016 founding by Dmitry Birukov and Pavel Potapov, now based in Yoshkar-Ola, Russia. Neither account traces to a primary company filing we could verify, so treat the company's origin story as unconfirmed rather than settled.

faq.question: Does Chaport integrate with Shopify or a CRM?
faq.answer: No dedicated Shopify integration or native CRM (Salesforce, HubSpot) sync was found. Chaport is built as a general-purpose live chat widget for any website rather than an ecommerce- or CRM-integrated platform, and its Zapier integration (Unlimited tier only) would be the realistic path to bridge either gap.

faq.question: Who is Chaport actually a good fit for?
faq.answer: Small businesses, solo operators, and simple websites that want an affordable, easy-to-set-up live chat widget with a basic FAQ bot, and don't have a specific need for AI-driven automation. If genuine AI resolution accuracy, automatic knowledge-base training, or agentic actions (order lookups, refunds) are what you're evaluating tools for, Chaport isn't built to compete on that axis at all.

pricingBreakdown: Chaport's pricing is straightforward and genuinely cheap relative to most tools on this site — a 4-operator team on Pro pays $29/month, and even the unlimited-operator Unlimited tier tops out at $99/month, both well under what a comparable seat count would cost on Help Scout, Front, or Intercom. The catch, and it's an important one, is that you're not buying the same category of product: there's no per-resolution AI fee anywhere in Chaport's pricing because there's no generative AI to meter. If you compare Chaport's $99/month Unlimited tier against Chatbase's $150/month Standard tier or Tidio's Lyro AI add-on, you're not actually comparing like-for-like capability — Chaport's price reflects a simpler, rule-based product, and the comparison only makes sense if a scripted FAQ bot genuinely meets your needs rather than a self-learning AI agent.

capabilities.note: The core product, and it does this job well and cheaply: a customizable widget, saved replies, pre-chat forms, and a genuinely useful native multi-language auto-detection feature that several pricier, AI-focused competitors don't build in natively. If your need is simply 'a chat box on my website,' this is a competent, affordable choice.

Real and functional, but it's important to be precise about what kind of 'chatbot' this is: a visual flow builder for scripting conversation paths with triggers and branching reply options, not a generative AI agent trained automatically on your content. Every conversation path has to be built by hand. If you've been comparing this against Chatbase, Tidio's Lyro, or any other LLM-based competitor expecting similar capability, recalibrate your expectations before buying.

A genuine standout given the product's simplicity and price: the widget auto-detects a visitor's language and switches without a paid add-on, which several more expensive, more AI-forward competitors in this category still don't offer natively.

Basic and tier-gated, with independent reviewers specifically flagging a lack of advanced reporting as a real limitation. Integration depth outside of WordPress and a top-tier-only Zapier connection is thin — no Shopify, no native CRM, no Wix or Squarespace app.

Worth noting directly: basic facts like founding year and location are genuinely unreconciled across available sources, which is unusual even for a small company and worth factoring into your confidence about long-term vendor stability and support continuity.

verdict: Chaport is an honest, competent product at what it actually is — a simple, affordable live chat widget with a scripted chatbot builder — and the mismatch is entirely about expectations, not execution. Independent reviewers who bought it for exactly that are genuinely happy: easy setup, good value against pricier competitors, and a native multi-language widget that several more expensive, AI-forward tools in this category still don't build in themselves. But the central thing worth being direct about is that Chaport's 'chatbot' is not a generative AI agent in the sense every other AI-native tool on this site is measured against: it's a visual flow builder for scripting decision-tree conversations with triggers and branching options, built by hand, not trained automatically on your content. There's no resolution-rate claim to evaluate because there's no generative model resolving anything, and there's no hallucination risk because there's nothing being generated. If you've been comparing Chaport's $99/month Unlimited tier against Chatbase, Tidio's Lyro, or any LLM-based competitor's pricing, you're not comparing equivalent products — Chaport is cheaper because it's doing meaningfully less, not because it's a hidden bargain on the same capability. My honest read: if your actual need is a cheap, easy, well-reviewed live chat widget with basic scripted automation and you have no specific requirement for genuine AI, Chaport does that job well and affordably. If any part of your evaluation criteria involves AI resolution accuracy, automatic training, or agentic actions, look elsewhere on this site — this isn't competing on that axis at all.
